title: Cylinder Commissioning & Paperwork | G3 Guide
description: Understand cylinder commissioning and installation paperwork with clear model-aware information and practical questions for your cylinder engineer.
answer: A commissioning checklist, a service record and Building Regulations notification serve different purposes. Establish the documentation appropriate to the specific installation.

sections.heading: The key distinction
paragraphs: The cylinder manual usually includes or refers to a commissioning record that captures the installed equipment and checks. The customer should receive the operating instructions and understand normal controls and safety escalation.

sections.heading: Apply the information to the installed system
paragraphs: Competent-person scheme members can self-certify covered work within their authorised scope. Otherwise the appropriate building-control route must be established. Holding unvented training alone should not be described as automatic scheme membership.

sections.heading: A practical next question
paragraphs: Gather the full model, heating method, recent symptoms and available paperwork. Discuss the scope with a person competent for the actual work. Technical information here supports that conversation and is not a substitute for manufacturer instructions or individual system assessment.

faqs.question: Does a completed service checklist replace installation notification?
faqs.answer: No. Maintenance records and Building Regulations notification have different purposes; the installer should explain the correct route for the installation work.
